To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we analyzed hESC enriched proteins using a network-based bioinformatic analysis to construct a protein-protein interaction network in order to learn how these proteins interact with each others in hESCs and to understand the functional significance of these proteins in hESCs.
we constructed a network of proteins and functional terms in hESCs using bioinformatics tools and that we found that the network is enriched in hESCs.

we have identified an hESC-en-riched protein interaction network, which is larger than random networks, and that we have identified a network of molecular functions that is over-represented within the hESC-enrich-ed protein interaction network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction and analysis of protein-protein interaction networks in human ES cells.
the construction of protein-protein interaction network and functional interaction network in human embryonic stems cells (hESCs).
the development of a computational approach to identify the protein interaction networks in human ES cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our network-based analysis of hESCs has revealed the molecular characteristics and functional significance of these cells, which will help us to understand the molecular basis of hESCs and may lead to new therapeutic applications.
we constructed a protein network of hESCs and identified functional enrichment in this network.

we have identified a protein-protein interaction network in hESCs which is enriched with hESC-enrich genes and which is also enriched with functional terms, suggesting the importance of these genes/proteins in hESCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the network of hESC-enrich proteins may be critical for maintaining and regulating hESCs.
by using protein-protein interaction and gene enrichment data, we have constructed a protein interaction and molecular functional network in hESCs.
by integrating protein-protein interaction network analysis and gene ontology analysis, we can identify the most critical proteins and their functions in hESCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the protein interaction network of hESCs is scale-free and that the hub proteins are likely to be regulated by transcription factors such as NANOG and SOX2, and that the functional interaction network may also be enriched in hESCs.
a protein interaction network can be a useful tool to identify important proteins and to understand the functional significance in hESCs.
the network-based bioinformatics approach is an effective tool for understanding the molecular characteristics of hESCs.
